Container.Name: Unraid-MCP
Container.Overview:
MCP server that lets MCP clients query and manage your Unraid server through the Unraid GraphQL API: system info, array and parity, disks, shares, Docker, VMs, notifications, plugins, rclone and live telemetry. Destructive actions require an explicit confirmation.
First launch: 1. In Unraid, open Settings › Management Access › API Keys, create a key and paste it in Unraid API key. 2. Set Unraid API URL to the GraphQL endpoint of the server, e.g. http://192.168.1.10/graphql. 3. Generate a token (openssl rand -hex 32 in the Unraid terminal) and paste it in MCP bearer token. 4. In your MCP client, add the streamable HTTP server http://UNRAID-IP:6970/mcp with the header Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN.
The server has no web page. It can stop the array, containers and VMs: never expose its port to the internet.
Container.Requires: The Unraid API: built into Unraid 7.2 and later; on older releases, install the Unraid Connect plugin first (no Unraid Connect sign-in needed for local access). The image is amd64 only.

Config.Name: Unraid API key
Config.Description: Key from Settings › Management Access › API Keys

Config.Name: MCP bearer token
Config.Description: Token MCP clients must send, e.g. from openssl rand -hex 32

Config.Name: UNRAID_MCP_PORT
Config.Description: Internal listen port (must match MCP Port container port)

Config.Name: UNRAID_VERIFY_SSL
Config.Description: Check the Unraid API certificate: true, false or path to a CA bundle

Config.Name: UNRAID_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS
Config.Description: Must be true to allow UNRAID_VERIFY_SSL=false

Config.Name: UNRAID_MCP_LOG_LEVEL
Config.Description: Log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR or CRITICAL
